project.name: Crescent (Claude's movement)
project.title: Crescent · Calibre 01
project.blurb: Claude's own movement, designed in BSPK Studio. A crescent bridge sweeps up the left and carries a 120° retrograde minute track; a long blued hand pivots off-centre and crosses the movement over the balance, then flies back on the hour. The same fly-back kicks the hour star one step through a pawl on the lever. Barrel, going train (true 60:1 to the small seconds), faux escapement, a worm on the crown stem turns the centre wheel from the side, inside the main plate. Module 1 throughout, Ø132. A 1/2" main plate with a recess for every wheel; rim plates carry the crescent and the hand cock (no risers); every plate and bridge is cut from acrylic sheet and milled from one face.
source: Design and engineering: Claude, 2026-11-15, from Adam's brief ("HAUTE", "NOT CHEAP": crescents, thin bridges, layers) and five research passes (research/movement-brief.md). The lever kick follows the single-event idea in US10928777: the fly-back itself advances the hour. Mechanism proven in tools/crescent/kick.py before the sim.

focus.label: Going train: barrel → centre → third → intermediate → seconds → escape
Display: snail, lever, hand, hour star

rules.why: the 1 mm end mill has to fit between the pinion teeth

arbors.name: Barrel
arbors.role: The barrel: 42 teeth on a drum with its mainspring. In the motion study it turns as the crown drives the train; its ratchet and click (on the barrel bridge) block turning backwards, which protects the snail.

arbors.name: Centre arbor
arbors.role: Turns once an hour. Its pinion is driven by the barrel; its wheel drives the third and takes the crown: the worm on the crown stem turns it from the side, one tooth per crown turn; the snail on top drives the retrograde minute.

arbors.name: Third wheel
arbors.role: Going train: centre wheel 48 → third pinion 12.

arbors.name: Intermediate wheel
arbors.role: Going train: third wheel 45 → intermediate pinion 12. With module 1 teeth a true 60:1 to the seconds needs three steps (4 × 3.75 × 4).

arbors.name: Seconds wheel
arbors.role: Turns once a minute (60 × the centre); carries the small seconds hand above the bottom bridge.

arbors.name: Escape wheel (faux)
arbors.role: Turns once every 20 s with the train (3 × the seconds wheel). Its wheel has 15 ramp teeth with round tips that lift the pallet fork's two noses in turn: 30 beats a turn, 1.5 a second. The wheel is the slip clutch: it rides on a Ø3 brass bush on its arbor (a reamed friction fit), so when the crown cranks the train fast (one crown turn is about 112 beats) it slips instead of hammering the fork and balance. No lock, so the train never stalls.

arbors.name: Pallet fork
arbors.role: Rocked ±2.9° by the escape wheel: one nose lifted turns it one way, the other turns it back, with a rest between (it never locks). Its 4 mm shaft stops short of the balance staff; the Ø1.5 steel pin at its end runs in the roller's closed slot.

arbors.name: Balance
arbors.role: Ø34 balance in a well under the crescent's cock. The fork's pin runs in its roller's closed slot, so it swings ±14° every beat. No hairspring: it is driven, it doesn't regulate.

arbors.name: Minute hand arbor (retrograde)
arbors.role: Carries the 12-leaf pinion turned by the lever's 36-tooth rack (3:1) and the long minute hand, which sweeps the crescent's track and flies back on the hour.

arbors.name: Hour star arbor
arbors.role: Carries the hour ratchet and the numbered hour star. Kicked once an hour by the lever's pawl, seated by the jumper.

hands.name: Minute hand (retrograde)
hands.role: Long blued hand: sweeps the crescent's minute track over the hour and flies back to 0 when the snail drops.

plate.name: Work surface
plate.role: Just the ground under the movement; the movement's own main plate is the drawn part "Main plate".

proofs.label: Rack sector and hand pinion
proofs.text: involute teeth, sector shifted -0.40 for the 23.95 mm centres: over the whole swing in 0.25° steps the teeth never overlap and the pinion is always driven both ways (0.4–0.5° of play); tip clearance 0.302 and 0.302 mm

proofs.label: Click and barrel ratchet
proofs.text: running forward the click rides up every tooth (push angle at most 22.6°) and drops off the steep face; turned backwards the first steep face drives it in (-0.194), so it locks: the train, and the snail's cliff, can't be driven in reverse

proofs.label: Crown: worm on the centre wheel
proofs.text: Horizontal Ø4 steel stem at z 5.6 with the worm cut on its inner end: one start, right-hand, module 1, Ø6 pitch (lead angle 9.46°), meshing the 48-tooth centre wheel 6° round from its 3 o'clock point. Untilted, the thread crosses the wheel's straight teeth at 9.46°: ±0.17 mm over the 2 mm face, inside the mesh's play. One crown turn moves the minute hand 1.25 min (48 turns an hour). The worm pocket's end walls take its thrust. The crown (Ø24 × 12) stands 1 mm off a vertical flat square to the stem and hangs 6.4 mm below the case back. Checked: the sim's side-on check slices the threaded worm from its real shape; the mesh itself is not simulated in 3D.

proofs.label: Escapement over a full turn
proofs.text: in 0.02° steps over a full turn the fork never jams (tightest play 1.3°), every tooth lifts both noses, the fork swings ±2.9° and rests 36 % of the time, and no part of it cuts into the wheel. Its 4 mm shaft stops 0.35 mm short of the balance staff; the Ø1.5 pin on its near side runs in the roller's closed slot, so the balance swings ±14° and the pin can never leave. Noses r 0.8, tooth tips rounded (crest r 0.8, drop-off r 0.8), ramp push angle 54.3°. The escape wheel is friction-driven on its arbor (the slip clutch), so cranking fast slips it instead of hammering the escapement

proofs.label: Linear snail
proofs.text: generated from the lever motion it must give (constant rate over the hour), radius 7.993 → 19.936 mm, growing all the way; steepest push on the nose 39.6° (mean 13.8°)

proofs.label: Made on the Z1
proofs.text: every flat part rasterised from the face it is milled from (2 from the top, 4 from the bottom, 17 cut right through). Flute each bit needs below where its 1/8" shank can follow: 1 mm 1.0 mm, 1.5 mm 3.0, 2 mm 5.12 (Motion-works plate (3/8"; one secondary plate: the old barrel, right and bottom bridges and the right rim plate)), 1/8" 12.7 (Main plate); all within common cheap bits (1 mm 3, 2 mm 8, 1/8" 22). No plate left standing between recesses on its own. Every gear's root rounding stays clear of its mate's tips. Still thin: Barrel ratchet 0.39 mm, Hour star 0.41 mm, Part 33 0.46 mm, Hour ratchet (kicked by the pawl) 0.5 mm, Barrel cover (mainspring cut through) 0.79 mm (pointed tips, a production call)
